scope: Supplemental 27 local commit objects. Messages and first-parent/root changed paths only; full semantic diffs not reviewed.

commits.message: WIP on main: 8d9044f Fit the ceiling to the window, and make a budget that can ask for less
docs(readme): precise nomenclature — loop / run mode (deterministic·hybrid·non-deterministic) / profile (step template); rebuild diagrams
WIP on main: 2895981 Repair the red CI gates and the pointers that had gone stale

Make the core dependency-free and the tabular domain optional

The package advertised `pip install taedri-loop[ml]`, which framed a universal
loop runtime as a machine-learning tool. The cause was structural rather than
cosmetic: __init__.py eagerly imported the tabular adapter, so numpy was a hard
dependency of the whole package and every user installed a scientific stack to
run a loop that never touches an array.

  - the core now has ZERO dependencies: loop runtime, four intelligence
    pillars, ledger, reports and every model provider are standard library;
  - the tabular/competition/RL adapters resolve lazily and keep their names;
  - `[ml]` becomes `[tabular]` — it is about TABLES, and it is one domain
    among others rather than the subject of the package. `[ml]` is kept as an
    alias so an existing install still resolves;
  - asking for an uninstalled adapter returns its install command, not a stack
    trace three frames down.

Verified in a clean virtualenv: `pip install taedri-loop` pulls nothing but
the package, and a loop, a report and the provider layer all run.

Runtime fix — `success_once` could stop with ZERO successes
  Reaching the end of the step sequence terminated the loop as "done"
  regardless of the stop condition. Under `success_once` that is wrong: the
  condition is "one iteration succeeded", so finishing without a success means
  going round again. A retry-until-it-works loop silently ran exactly one
  attempt and reported success. It now retries, and a never-succeeding loop
  stops on budget and says so rather than claiming completion. Found by
  writing the example for it; regression test covers all three cases.

Examples: 4 -> 6
  05_kaggle_competition.py  a real competition end to end, optional submission
  06_your_own_loop.py       your steps, your stop condition, your domain —
                            invoice reconciliation, no dependencies, no data
                            science
  examples/README.md        which example needs what, and the two traps worth
                            knowing (a store hit outranks a model call; the
                            stop condition is a real choice)

Excluded two commercial-strategy documents from the public repository; they
describe the business rather than the library and stay in the private tree.

Suite 908 in-tree / 905 from a clean [tabular] install, all gates pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

A universal front door: say what you want, it works out the rest

The complaint that drove this: "this loop should be intelligent enough to
figure out any solution; a user shouldn't have to tell it that it is a tabular
task unless the user wants to." Correct. The old entry point made the caller do
the orienting — train_csv, test_csv, sample_csv, out_csv — so you had to know
it was tabular, which files played which role, and that a submission template
existed. All of that can be asked of the data.

    solve("work out which accounts will renew", data="./mydata")

Orientation is INSPECTION at zero model calls: modality from what files are
actually present, identifier from uniqueness, target from structure, problem
type from the target's own values. Every conclusion carries its evidence, so a
caller can disagree — and any field can be passed explicitly, which always
wins and is recorded as an override. Inference is the default; the override is
optional. An ambiguous task reports low confidence instead of picking a
plausible default and sounding certain.

ONE front door, three routes: data -> orient and execute; no data -> the
knowledge solver; a shape with no executor -> oriented, reported, and honestly
not solved. `loop.solver.solve` is no longer re-exported as `solve`; two public
functions of that name is the confusion this removes.

Target detection is structural, not a word list
  The detector had `churn` in its list. A real corpus said `renewed`, so the
  target was missed and the run worked by accident — a closed list answering
  "nothing found" for everything it was never told about, while reading like a
  measurement. Now: present-in-train-absent-from-test, then the caller's own
  goal text ("will renew" reaches the column `renewed`), then cardinality, with
  names as the weakest tie-break.

Never train on your own output
  Running solve() twice into the same folder made the second run read the
  first run's predictions as training data. Output-shaped files are excluded
  and the exclusion is reported.

Also in this change
  - knowledge_loader: .md .txt .csv .tsv .json .jsonl .py .yaml become
    searchable intelligence. Markdown splits at headings, Python docstrings
    make a codebase searchable by what it says it does, every record traces to
    its file and position, ids are stable across reloads, and anything
    unreadable is REPORTED — the store previously swallowed every parse error
    and returned an empty store with no error at all.
  - guided_setup: `taedri-loop setup` checks each step by performing it, in
    the deterministic -> hybrid -> model-backed order, and ends by running a
    real loop and printing its report. Non-interactive stdin never blocks.
  - README rebuilt on the imported design system: mermaid diagrams for the
    loop, the mode ladder, spawn trees and the four intelligence surfaces,
    using the project's own palette. Extras are reframed as library WEIGHT
    rather than task type, because you never tell the loop what kind of task
    you have.
  - sync_to_standalone.sh: the monorepo is the source, this repo is a
    projection. Hand-copying files silently reverted a change once and no test
    caught it, because both trees were internally consistent and disagreed
    with each other.
  - optional adapters no longer look like failures: a test that cannot run
    reports requires_extra with its install command, counted separately, and
    the map-import check distinguishes real drift from an uninstalled adapter.
  - docs/internal/HANDOFF.md: state, enforced rules, non-obvious conventions,
    and open work ranked.

934/934 full · 895/895 with ZERO dependencies · 19/19 gates · clean-install
verified.

fix: PEP 701 f-string broke Python 3.10/3.11, and add the gate for it

A multi-line expression inside an f-string is PEP 701 — valid on 3.12+ and a
SyntaxError on the 3.10 this package declares support for. A 3.14 workstation
parsed it happily, the full suite passed locally, and it failed only in CI on
the two oldest matrix entries, after the push.

  - fixed the f-string in knowledge_loader;
  - added a zero-tolerance gate (now 20) that parses every module with the
    OLDEST installed interpreter, rather than trusting the current one. Where
    no older interpreter exists it reports nothing rather than passing — a
    check that cannot run has established nothing;
  - the gate was verified by REINTRODUCING the exact bug and confirming it is
    caught, then restoring;
  - _conformance_scan is declared in subprocess_allowed_modules with its
    reason: detecting syntax the current interpreter accepts requires invoking
    a different one.

934/934, 20/20 gates.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Initial release: taedri-loop 0.1.0

One recursive Loop. Search, advice, model calls, adapters, validators and whole
solutions all execute inside the same envelope, so any of them can be nested,
retried, budgeted, replaced or inspected without special cases. A run produces
its work and its evidence together.

Layout
  src/taedri_loop/   the package (loop, strings, code_nodes, static_architecture)
  src/taedri.py      short import alias — a MODULE, not a package, so it cannot
                     duplicate submodules
  docs/              getting started, four guides, architecture, reference,
                     evidence receipts, and internal development artifacts
  examples/          four runnable programs

Providers
  Ollama Cloud, Mistral and OpenRouter behind one contract, plus custom_endpoint
  — a single parameterised adapter for any OpenAI-compatible or Ollama-native
  server. Discovery classifies live catalogs into roles at zero model calls from
  vendor-declared facts, stamped basis="declared", measured=False. configure()
  verifies every provider by a real call and reports which loop modes this
  installation can actually run, before a job starts.

Reporting
  Loop reports in text, Markdown, HTML and JSON, projected from the run's own
  ledger — never recomputed from another source. CLI: --runs, --report,
  --format, --out. The tree is built from the parentage the runtime records, so
  a loop of loops renders as one.

Verification
  907 offline tests and 19 zero-tolerance conformance gates, neither of which
  touches the network or can bill a provider. Verified from a clean virtual
  environment: 904/904 with `[ml]`, the two uninstalled extras reported as a
  named category with their install commands rather than as failures.

Defects found by clean-install and live-model testing, each with a regression
test:
  - the taedri alias forwarded __path__, so `import taedri.loop.recursive_loop`
    loaded a SECOND copy of the module — two objects, two states;
  - four runtime data files were absent from package-data, so the suite failed
    only after installation;
  - studio_server.self_test indexed a saved run that does not exist on a fresh
    clone; it passed only because earlier runs were lying around on disk;
  - loop reports read only `init` for parentage, rendering genuinely nested runs
    as a flat list and hiding the one structure a report exists to show.

MIT licensed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
